Operations is the connective tissue of every business. Every department's work eventually flows through operations — approvals, reporting, vendor management, IT support, process documentation.

When operations runs on manual processes, every department slows down. When operations runs on automated workflows, every department moves faster.

We published a piece this week that maps the five operations workflows where AI delivers the fastest impact — with actual trigger-action sequences and a 30-day implementation plan.

The 3-question framework for identifying automatable workflows is the part I keep sharing with founders:

1. Does this workflow follow the same steps every time it runs?
2. Is the trigger clearly defined?
3. Is the output clearly defined?

If a workflow passes all three, it is ready to automate. If it fails any of them, define the missing element before building.

Simple framework. Saves a lot of wasted automation effort.

twitter_thread: Operations is the connective tissue of every business. When it runs on manual processes, every department slows down. When it runs on automated workflows, every department moves faster. Here are the 5 workflows to automate first:

Workflow 1 — Cross-department reporting: Monday 7am, data pulled from all connected systems, normalized, formatted into 3 versions (exec summary, dept breakdown, full data), distributed automatically. 4-6 hours recovered per team member per week.

Workflow 2 — IT tier-1 support: ticket created → classified → resolution runbook checked → if known, automated response sent or action taken → if novel, routed to engineer with context. 60-70% of IT tickets resolved without human involvement.

Workflow 3 — Approval routing: request submitted → classified → routed to correct approver(s) → one-click approve/reject via Slack → approved = next step triggered → no response in 48 hours = escalated. Standard approvals in 4-8 hours vs. 2-5 business days.

Workflow 4 — Vendor management: 90-day renewal alerts, automated invoice matching against contract terms, quarterly review scheduling, performance data pulled automatically. No more spreadsheet that is perpetually out of date.

Workflow 5 — Compliance tracking: deadline monitoring, 30/14/7-day reminders, automated evidence collection for SOC 2 and ISO 27001, completion reports generated automatically. Compliance that runs on schedule regardless of how busy the week was.
